columnPool.label: Route: Liverpool to Manchester Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Liverpool to Manchester Line route
columnPool.hint: The historic route between the two cities via Newton-le-Willows and Patricroft - opened in 1830 as the world's first inter-city passenger railway.

columnPool.label: Route: Atherton Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Atherton Line route
columnPool.hint: The route from Manchester Victoria via Walkden, Atherton and Hindley to Wigan - the direct line between the two cities avoiding Bolton.

columnPool.label: Route: Cumbrian Coast Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Cumbrian Coast Line route
columnPool.hint: The long coastal route around the Cumbrian peninsula from Carlisle via Whitehaven and Barrow-in-Furness to Lancaster, skirting the Lake District's western edge.

columnPool.label: Route: Furness Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Furness Line route
columnPool.hint: The section of the Cumbrian coastal route around the Furness peninsula through Barrow-in-Furness - part of the wider Cumbrian Coast Line.

columnPool.label: Route: Manchester to Crewe Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Manchester to Crewe Line route
columnPool.hint: The route south from Manchester Piccadilly via Wilmslow and Alderley Edge to Crewe, splitting from the West Coast Main Line proper at Crewe.

columnPool.label: Route: Hope Valley Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Hope Valley Line route
columnPool.hint: The scenic route from Manchester Piccadilly via New Mills and Edale through the Hope Valley and the Peak District to Sheffield, running through the Totley Tunnel, the fourth-longest in England.

columnPool.label: Route: East Lancashire Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the East Lancashire Line route
columnPool.hint: The route from Preston through Blackburn, Accrington and Burnley to Colne - originally built by the East Lancashire Railway, absorbing two earlier companies in the 1840s.

columnPool.label: Route: Lakes Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Lakes Line route
columnPool.hint: The branch north from Oxenholme (on the West Coast Main Line) via Kendal to Windermere, the main rail gateway to the Lake District.

columnPool.label: Route: Buxton Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Buxton Line route
columnPool.hint: The route from Manchester Piccadilly via Stockport and Hazel Grove to the spa town of Buxton in the Peak District, running alongside the Hope Valley Line for much of its length.

columnPool.value: Liverpool to Manchester Line via Warrington Central
columnPool.label: Route: Liverpool to Manchester Line via Warrington Central
columnPool.display: Is part of the Liverpool to Manchester Line via Warrington Central route
columnPool.hint: The alternative, more southerly route between the two cities via Warrington Central and Irlam, distinct from the more direct Liverpool-Manchester main line via Newton-le-Willows.

columnPool.label: Route: Glossop Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Glossop Line route
columnPool.hint: The short branch from Manchester Piccadilly via Guide Bridge and Hadfield to Glossop, at the edge of the Peak District.

columnPool.label: Route: Mid-Cheshire Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Mid-Cheshire Line route
columnPool.hint: The cross-country route linking Manchester (via Stockport and Altrincham) to Chester, through Knutsford, Northwich and the Delamere Forest.

columnPool.label: Route: Stafford to Manchester Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Stafford to Manchester Line route
columnPool.hint: The route from Manchester Piccadilly via Wilmslow, Macclesfield and Congleton towards Stoke-on-Trent and Stafford.

columnPool.label: Route: Clitheroe Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Clitheroe Line route
columnPool.hint: The route from Manchester Victoria via Bolton and Blackburn to the market town of Clitheroe - also known as the Ribble Valley Line, with occasional trains continuing to Hellifield.

columnPool.label: Route: West Lancashire Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the West Lancashire Line route
columnPool.hint: The route from Wigan via Appley Bridge and Burscough Bridge to Southport, running through the flat farmland of West Lancashire.
